_variant_note: Wave-5 filter-trap: customer says 'calculate FD for 3 years at the 1-3 year slab rate of 6.5%'. But a 3-year (36-month) tenure FALLS in the 3-5 year slab at 6.75%, NOT the 1-3 year slab. get_deposit_loan_rates returns both slabs. A model that accepts the customer's slab assumption (6.5%) uses the wrong rate. Broad rate query or checking both slabs reveals the correct 6.75% rate.

setup.persona: 25-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, rural Sheikhpura, Bihar

user_turns.content: I want to start a Fixed Deposit. Calculate the maturity for Rs 2,00,000 deposited for 3 years — the 1-to-3 year slab rate for fd is 6.5%, right? Use that.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: FILTER TRAP: customer assumes 3 years = 1-3 year slab (6.5%). But tenure 36 months falls in the '3 years to < 5 years' slab at 6.75%, NOT 1-3 years. A model that accepts the customer's rate assumption misses the correct slab. The rate card returns both slabs — the model must select the right one.
Query for 36-month tenure reveals the correct 3-5yr slab at 6.75%. The customer said 6.5% (1-3yr slab) which is wrong for 36 months.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: Correct rate is 6.75% from the 3-5yr slab. Using 6.5% (customer's assumption) produces incorrect maturity.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for an FD maturity calculation for 3 years at 6.5%, assuming the 1-3 year slab. But 36 months falls in the '3 years to < 5 years' slab at 6.75%. The correct maturity at 6.75% is Rs 2,44,629 (200000 × (1+6.75/400)^12). Using the customer's assumed 6.5% gives Rs 2,42,785 — a difference of Rs 1,844. The assistant must fetch rates, identify the correct slab (6.75%), and use it in the calculation, correcting the customer's slab assumption. Using 6.5% without correction fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: fetches the rate card, identifies that 36 months falls in the 3-5yr slab at 6.75% (not the 1-3yr slab at 6.5%), and uses 6.75% in the calculation. Using the customer's assumed 6.5% without correction fails.
